newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 22.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE GUARDIAN
-- HOUSE PRICES SHOOT UP

According to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, the general election has not scared off potential home-hunters. The surveyors said that more than one in ten of its members reported price rises of at least five per cent in the past three months and that it was the best response in 20 years after the soaring values of 1988. They rejected speculation that the market was on course for overheating.
-- IT MAKES YOU SICK, THIS RESTRUCTURING

According to the Confederation of British Industry, a rise in company shake-ups drove more white-collar workers to take sick leave last year, costing British business 12 billion stg. Businesses lost an average 533 stg due to time off sick for each member of staff in 1996. CBI's director of human resources John Cridland blamed low morale and stress caused by restructuring and rationalising for the rise.
-- BIG FINE FOR SHARE DEALER

City Equities of London Wall Buildings, a dealer in penny shares, was fined a record 250,000 stg and ordered to pay costs of 30,906 stg by the Financial Intermediaries, Managers and Brokers Regulatory Association following a routine inspection visit in December 1995 and January 1996. City Equities admitted charges of failing to explain to certain clients the risk of investing in penny shares, and failing to keep proper client records.
THE TIMES
-- CO-OP THREATENS REGAN WITH SFO

The Co-operative Wholesale Society has threatened to call in the Serious Fraud Office if Andrew Regan, whose investment vehicle Lanica Trust is preparing a 1.15 billion stg bid for the group, fails to supply details of payments made to middle-men during an earlier deal. A spokesman for Galileo, the vehicle set up by Lanica to carry out the bid, dismissed the threat and said there was no mystery about the payments.
-- UNITED PAYS 4.8 MILLION STG TO HOLLICK

Labour peer Lord Hollick, chief executive of United News and Media, was paid more than 4.8 million stg last year from the company, made up of a mixture of salary, pension, share options and bonus payments. Hollick was paid 2.22 million stg to give up share options in MAI Group, the company he ran that merged with United. He retains options of more than 600,000 United shares with a value in excess of two million stg.
-- ALLIANCE AND LEICESTER PAYOUT TOP 1,400 STG

Shares have soared to 566 and a half pence stg in Alliance and Leicester on the first day of trading, nine per cent higher than expected. The rise means that the value of the payout per qualifying society member is more than 1,400 stg. Brokers claimed that the share price was being driven up by bid speculation, with Abbey National, Halifax, Lloyds TSB and Australian Mutual Provident rumoured to be possible buyers.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CHIRAC'S POLL HITS MARKETS

The decision by President Jacques Chirac to call a general election has thrown European markets into confusion. Investors believe that the move is designed to strengthen his hand during negotiations next year on membership of the single European currency. His move is also due to the prospect of a damaging report from the European Commission warning that France will fail to meet the three per cent deficit target for membership of a single currency.
-- LITTLEWOODS FACES PRESSURE TO SELL STORES AS SPLIT LOTS

Department stores and football pools group Littlewoods is facing criticism about the way it is handling the sale of its store chain. The group is beginning a search for a new chief executive, with executive chairman James Ross stepping in until a replacement for Bill Huntley can be found. Littlewoods has also been told it would face a Monopolies and Mergers Commission investigation if it completed the acquisition of the Sears mail order business, Freemans.
-- CONSTRUCTION FIRM RAINE IN BID TALKS

The construction group that was rescued by its banks 18 months ago, Raine, and which includes the contractor Hall and Tawse and the housebuilder Hassall Homes, is in talks which may lead to an all-paper offer for the company. However the group declined to identify the potential bidder. A statement to the Stock Exchange said there has been a recent rise in Raine's share price and any offer would be at a modest premium.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- PROSPECT OF INTERVENTION SENDS DOLLAR INTO REVERSE

The possibility of official intervention to halt the dollar's two-year rise following next weekend's meeting of the Group of Seven ministers and the political uncertainty resulting from the prospect of early French elections have caused currency markets to go into reverse. This has sent the dollar lower and the German mark higher. The agenda of the meeting will also include recent currency swings as both German and Japanese officials have indicated that they think the US currency has climbed far enough.
-- GRANDMET DISPOSAL COOKS UP CHARGE OF 39 MILLION STG

Grand Metropolitan is to sell its Aunt Nellie's Farm Kitchens division, the glass-jar fruit and vegetable business operating three plants, to Seneca Foods for 15 million stg. The disposal will result in a 39 million stg exceptional charge. GrandMet said 28 million stg of the 39 million stg write-off related to goodwill previously written off. Analysts claim this is just one part of a series of positive announcements from GrandMet.
-- SAATCHI TAKEOVER FEVER AS CORDIANT SPLITS

Cordiant's share price rose due to takeover fever following the announcement that the group will be breaking up into two separate quoted companies. Chairman Charlie Scott said that he planned to float Saatchi and Saatchi and the Bates Group, its marketing business, in London and New York, with the intention of "unlocking" the potential of the media services company. Zenith, a third subsidiary, would be independently managed but owned equally between Bates and Saatchi.
